ai.definition: Xenobiology is a field of synthetic biology that involves the creation of life forms using non-canonical amino acids or nucleic acids, which are not found in nature. These xenobiotic organisms can potentially perform functions that natural life cannot.
ai.howItWorks: The process begins by engineering ribosomes and polymerases to be capable of processing unnatural building blocks. This is achieved through genetic modifications that allow the synthetic cells to incorporate these non-canonical components into their proteins or nucleic acids, thereby altering their properties and potentially enabling new functions.
ai.problemSolved: Xenobiology addresses the limitations of natural life by providing a platform for creating organisms with novel biochemical capabilities. This can lead to breakthroughs in biocatalysis, where enzymes or other biological molecules are used to accelerate chemical reactions that would otherwise be slow or unfeasible under natural conditions.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves genetic engineering techniques and cell culture methods. It requires precise control over the synthesis of unnatural building blocks and their integration into the xenobiological system.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes designing the genetic modifications, synthesizing the non-canonical components, introducing them into host cells, and optimizing the expression and function of the resulting xenobiotic organisms.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the complexity of genetic engineering, the need for specialized equipment to synthesize and incorporate unnatural building blocks, and the rigorous testing required to ensure safety and efficacy.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: promising early-stage research with potential for significant breakthroughs in the future.
ai.regulation: Currently, there are no specific regulations for xenobiology, but it is closely monitored by regulatory bodies due to its potential risks and ethical considerations. Guidelines are being developed to ensure safety and prevent unintended consequences.
ai.risks: Risks include the potential for unintended release of xenobiotic organisms into the environment, which could disrupt ecosystems or pose health hazards. There are also concerns about the misuse of this technology in bioterrorism.
ai.profitability: Profitability is currently uncertain due to the early stage of development and lack of widespread applications. However, if successful, it could lead to significant commercial opportunities in areas such as pharmaceuticals, materials science, and biocatalysis.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include more efficient methods for synthesizing non-canonical components, improved host systems, and broader applications across various industries.

glossary.def: The study of life forms using non-natural building blocks.
Cellular structures responsible for protein synthesis in living organisms.
Enzymes that synthesize nucleic acids, such as DNA or RNA.

subsystems.name: Unnatural genetic polymer
subsystems.role: stores genetic information in a non-natural alphabet, either as an expanded base pair or a xeno-nucleic acid (XNA) backbone.

subsystems.name: Replication and transcription machinery
subsystems.role: copies and transcribes the unnatural genetic material with high fidelity.

subsystems.name: Orthogonal translation system
subsystems.role: incorporates non-canonical amino acids (ncAAs) into proteins at defined positions.

subsystems.name: Metabolic supply and transport
subsystems.role: delivers or synthesises the unnatural building blocks inside the cell.

subsystems.name: Containment and safety
subsystems.role: prevents the organism from surviving or spreading outside controlled conditions.

buildSteps.title: Design the unnatural building block
buildSteps.detail: Choose or synthesise a base pair or amino acid that is chemically stable, orthogonal to natural biochemistry, and compatible with polymerases or the ribosome.

buildSteps.title: Engineer enzymes to recognise it
buildSteps.detail: Use directed evolution and rational design to adapt polymerases, synthetases and other enzymes so they accept the unnatural substrate without losing fidelity.

buildSteps.title: Build an orthogonal translation system
buildSteps.detail: Create tRNA/synthetase pairs that charge only the non-canonical amino acid and suppress a dedicated codon, and modify the ribosome if needed for efficient incorporation.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the chassis cell
buildSteps.detail: Introduce the unnatural building block, transporters and engineered machinery into a robust host such as Escherichia coli, keeping the new chemistry separate from natural metabolism.

buildSteps.title: Optimise and evolve
buildSteps.detail: Adapt the organism to grow and replicate with the unnatural component, improving uptake, retention, fidelity and yield over many generations.

buildSteps.title: Test containment
buildSteps.detail: Verify that the organism depends on the supplied unnatural nutrient and cannot survive if it escapes, using auxotrophy and kill switches.

buildSteps.title: Apply for biocatalysis
buildSteps.detail: Engineer metabolic pathways that use the expanded chemistry to produce novel enzymes, polymers or small molecules not possible with standard biology.

prerequisites.tech: Synthetic chemistry for unnatural nucleotides and amino acids
prerequisites.why: researchers can already synthesise many modified bases, sugars and amino acids in the laboratory.
some XNA polymers can be copied in the lab, but efficiency and fidelity remain far below natural DNA replication.

prerequisites.tech: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs for multiple ncAAs
prerequisites.why: single ncAAs are routinely incorporated, but doing so for many different ncAAs simultaneously is still limited.
modified ribosomes can incorporate a few ncAAs, but broad tolerance and high yield are not yet demonstrated.
auxotrophy and kill switches work in principle, but escape or mutation remains a concern for environmental release.
a reduced genome would simplify xenobiological systems, but the minimal gene set for robust growth is not fully defined.

pathway.milestone: lab strains with one unnatural base pair and a handful of non-canonical amino acids
pathway.unlocks: proof that expanded genetic and protein alphabets can be maintained in living cells.

pathway.milestone: organisms with multiple unnatural base pairs and dozens of ncAAs
pathway.unlocks: synthesis of novel biopolymers and enzymes with new catalytic functions.

pathway.milestone: robust containment and scalable fermentation for xenobiological cells
pathway.unlocks: safe industrial use of xenobiology for biocatalysis and materials production.

pathway.milestone: commercial production of chemicals, drugs or materials using xenobiological organisms
pathway.unlocks: a new manufacturing platform that extends biology beyond its natural building blocks.
